newsitem.title: FRENCH GUIANA: Ariane rocket to launch two satellites Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Ariane rocket to launch two satellites Tuesday.

text.p: Western Europe's 97th Ariane rocket is scheduled to blast off from French Guiana on Tuesday carrying two communications satellites, the Arianespace company said on Monday.

The INMARSAT-3F4 satellite will provide mobile telecommunications in the western Atlantic ocean region for the London-based International Maritime Satellite Organisation (INMARSAT). The satellite was built in the U.S. by Lockheed Martin.
INSAT-2D, built in India by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) will provide telecommunications throughout India and neigbouring countries.
An Ariane 44L rocket equipped with four liquid strap-on boosters -- the most powerful in the Ariane-4 series -- will be used to launch the satellites that have a combined weight of 4.1 tonnes.

The launch is set for between 7.58 p.m. and 8.59 p.m. local time (2258 and 2359 GMT) from the European Space Agency (ESA) launch centre in Kourou, French Guiana on the northeast coast of South America.
The Paris-based Arianespace company that launches the Ariane rocket series said it had firm orders to launch 40 heavy satellites worth an estimated $3.3. billion.
